text_en: Now I would remind you, brothers and sisters, of the good news that I proclaimed to you, which you in turn received, in which also you stand,
text_cn: 弟兄们！我愿意你们认清，我们先前给你们所传报的福音，这福音你们已接受了，且在其上站稳了；

text_en: through which also you are being saved, if you hold firmly to the message that I proclaimed to you—unless you have come to believe in vain.
text_cn: 假使你们照我给你们所传报的话持守了福音，就必因这福音得救，否则，你们就白白地信了。

text_en: For I handed on to you as of first importance what I in turn had received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the scriptures,
text_cn: 我当日把我所领受而又传授给你们的，其中首要的是：基督照经上记载的，为我们的罪死了，

text_en: and that he was buried, and that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the scriptures,
text_cn: 被埋葬了，且照经上记载的，第三天复活了，

text_en: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
text_cn: 并且显现给刻法，以后显现给那十二位；

text_en: Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have died.
text_cn: 此后，又一同显现给五百多弟兄，其中多半到现在还活着，有些已经死了。

text_en: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
text_cn: 随后，显现给雅各伯，以后，显现给众宗徒；

text_en: Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me.
text_cn: 最后，也显现了给我这个像流产儿的人。

text_en: For I am the least of the apostles, unfit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
text_cn: 我原是宗徒中最小的一个，不配称为宗徒，因为我迫害过天主的教会。

text_en: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me has not been in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them—though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me.
text_cn: 然而，因天主的恩宠，我成为今日的我；天主赐给我的恩宠没有落空，我比他们众人更劳碌；其实不是我，而是天主的恩宠偕同我。

text_en: Whether then it was I or they, so we proclaim and so you have come to believe.
text_cn: 总之，不拘是我，或是他们，我们都这样传了，你们也都这样信了。

text_en: Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
text_cn: 我们既然传报了基督已由死者中复活了，怎么你们中还有人说：死人复活是没有的事呢？

text_en: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised;
text_cn: 假如死人复活是没有的事，基督也就没有复活；

text_en: and if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation has been in vain and your faith has been in vain.
text_cn: 假如基督没有复活，那么，我们的宣讲便是空的，你们的信仰也是空的。

text_en: We are even found to be misrepresenting God, because we testified of God that he raised Christ—whom he did not raise if it is true that the dead are not raised.
text_cn: 此外，如果死人真不复活，我们还被视为天主的假证人，因为我们相反天主作证，说天主使基督复活了，其实并没有使他复活，

text_en: For if the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised.
text_cn: 因为如果死人不复活，基督也就没有复活；

text_en: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile and you are still in your sins.
text_cn: 如果基督没有复活，你们的信仰便是假的，你们还是在罪恶中。

text_en: Then those also who have died in Christ have perished.
text_cn: 那么，那些在基督内死了的人，就丧亡了。

text_en: If for this life only we have hoped in Christ, we are of all people most to be pitied.
text_cn: 如果我们只在今生寄望于基督，我们就是众人中最可怜的了。

text_en: But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have died.
text_cn: 但是，基督从死者中实在复活了，做了死者的初果。

text_en: For since death came through a human being, the resurrection of the dead has also come through a human being;
text_cn: 因为死亡既因一人而来，死者的复活也因一人而来；

text_en: for as all die in Adam, so all will be made alive in Christ.
text_cn: 就如在亚当内，众人都死了，照样，在基督内，众人都要复活；

text_en: But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then at his coming those who belong to Christ.
text_cn: 不过各人要依照自己的次第：首先是为初果的基督，然后是在基督再来时属于基督的人，

text_en: Then comes the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, after he has destroyed every ruler and every authority and power.
text_cn: 再后才是结局；那时，基督将消灭一切率领者、一切掌权者和大能者，把自己的王权交于天主父。

text_en: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
text_cn: 因为基督必须为王，直到把一切仇敌屈服在他的脚下。

text_en: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
text_cn: 最后被毁灭的仇敌更是死亡；

text_en: For “God has put all things in subjection under his feet. ” But when it says, “All things are put in subjection, ” it is plain that this does not include the one who put all things in subjection under him.
text_cn: 因为天主使万物都屈服在他的脚下。既然说万物都已屈服了，显然那使万物屈服于他的不在其内。

text_en: When all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to the one who put all things in subjection under him, so that God may be all in all.
text_cn: 万物都屈服于他以后，子自己也要屈服于那使万物屈服于自己的父，好叫天主成为万物之中的万有。

text_en: Otherwise, what will those people do who receive baptism on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized on their behalf?
text_cn: 不然，那些代死人受洗的是作什么呢？如果死人总不复活，为什么还代他们受洗呢？

text_en: And why are we putting ourselves in danger every hour?
text_cn: 我们又为什么时时冒险呢？

text_en: I die every day! That is as certain, brothers and sisters, as my boasting of you—a boast that I make in Christ Jesus our Lord.
text_cn: 弟兄们，我指着我在我们的主基督耶稣内，对你们所有的荣耀，起誓说：我是天天冒死的。

text_en: If with merely human hopes I fought with wild animals at Ephesus, what would I have gained by it? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. ”
text_cn: 我若只凭人的动机，当日在厄弗所与野兽搏斗，为我有什么益处？如果死人不复活，“我们吃喝吧！明天就要死了。”

text_en: Do not be deceived: “Bad company ruins good morals. ”
text_cn: 你们不可为人所误：“交结恶友必败坏善行。”你们当彻底醒悟，别再犯罪了。

text_en: Come to a sober and right mind, and sin no more; for some people have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
text_cn: 你们中有些人实在不认识天主了：我说这话是为叫你们羞愧。

text_en: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body do they come? ”
text_cn: 可是有人要说：死人将怎样复活呢？他们将带着什么样的身体回来呢？

text_en: Fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
text_cn: 糊涂人哪！你所播的种子若不先死了，决不得生出来；

text_en: And as for what you sow, you do not sow the body that is to be, but a bare seed, perhaps of wheat or of some other grain.
text_cn: 并且你所播种的，并不是那将要生出的形体，而是一颗赤裸的籽粒，譬如一颗麦粒，或者别的种粒；

text_en: But God gives it a body as he has chosen, and to each kind of seed its own body.
text_cn: 但天主随自己的心意给它一个形体，使每个种子各有各的本体。

text_en: Not all flesh is alike, but there is one flesh for human beings, another for animals, another for birds, and another for fish.
text_cn: 不是所有的肉体都是同样的肉体：人体是一样，兽体又是一样，鸟体另是一样，鱼体却又另是一样。

text_en: There are both heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly is one thing, and that of the earthly is another.
text_cn: 还有天上的物体和地上的物体：天上物体的华丽是一样，地上物体的华丽又是一样；

text_en: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; indeed, star differs from star in glory.
text_cn: 太阳的光辉是一样，月亮的光辉又是一样，星辰的光辉另是一样；而且星辰与星辰的光辉又有分别。

text_en: So it is with the resurrection of the dead. What is sown is perishable, what is raised is imperishable.
text_cn: 死人的复活也是这样：播种的是可朽坏的，复活起来的是不可朽坏的；

text_en: It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power.
text_cn: 播种的是可羞辱的，复活起来的是光荣的；播种的是软弱的，复活起来的是强健的；

text_en: It is sown a physical body, it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a physical body, there is also a spiritual body.
text_cn: 播种的是属生灵的身体，复活起来的是属神的身体；既有属生灵的身体，也就有属神的身体。

text_en: Thus it is written, “The first man, Adam, became a living being”; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
text_cn: 经上也这样记载说：“第一个人亚当成了生灵，”最后的亚当成了使人生活的神。

text_en: But it is not the spiritual that is first, but the physical, and then the spiritual.
text_cn: 但属神的不是在先，而是属生灵的，然后才是属神的。

text_en: The first man was from the earth, a man of dust; the second man is from heaven.
text_cn: 第一个人出于地，属于土，第二个人出于天。

text_en: As was the man of dust, so are those who are of the dust; and as is the man of heaven, so are those who are of heaven.
text_cn: 那属于土的怎样，凡属于土的也怎样；那属于天上的怎样，凡属于天上的也怎样。

text_en: Just as we have borne the image of the man of dust, we will also bear the image of the man of heaven.
text_cn: 我们怎样带了那属于土的肖像，也要怎样带那属于天上的肖像。

text_en: What I am saying, brothers and sisters, is this: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
text_cn: 弟兄们，我告诉你们：肉和血不能承受天主的国，可朽坏的也不能承受不可朽坏的。

text_en: Listen, I will tell you a mystery! We will not all die, but we will all be changed,
text_cn: 看，我告诉你们一件奥秘的事：我们众人不全死亡，但我们众人却全要改变，

text_en: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
text_cn: 这是在顷刻眨眼之间，在末次吹号筒时发生的。的确，号筒一响，死人必要复活，成为不朽的，我们也必要改变，

text_en: For this perishable body must put on imperishability, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
text_cn: 因为这可朽坏的，必须穿上不可朽坏的；这可死的，必须穿上不可死的。

text_en: When this perishable body puts on imperishability, and this mortal body puts on immortality, then the saying that is written will be fulfilled: “Death has been swallowed up in victory. ”
text_cn: 几时这可朽坏的，穿上了不可朽坏的；这可死的，穿上了不可死的，那时就要应验经上所记载的这句话：“在胜利中，死亡被吞灭了。”

text_en: “Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting? ”
text_cn: “死亡！你的胜利在哪里？死亡！你的刺在哪里？”

text_en: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
text_cn: 死亡的刺就是罪过，罪过的权势就是法律。

text_en: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
text_cn: 感谢天主赐给了我们因我们的主耶稣基督所获得的胜利。

text_en: Therefore, my beloved, be steadfast, immovable, always excelling in the work of the Lord, because you know that in the Lord your labor is not in vain.
text_cn: 所以，我亲爱的弟兄，你们要坚定不移，在主的工程上该时常发愤勉力，因为你们知道，你们的勤劳在主内决不会落空。
